_comment: FCS saturation calculator for the emtk window: the controls of view.json (the AutoForm spec the Qt tool rendered) drawn by emtk.view_form over SaturationPanel (gui/panel.py). The state diagram and the plots are drawn by gui/app.py.

buttons.label: Compute
buttons.description: Recompute the FCS curves, the one-component and two-component fits, the radial profiles and the power sweeps from the current kinetics and optics. The plots also follow every edit.

buttons.label: Load scheme
buttons.description: Load a photophysical scheme (states, labels, transition rates and brightness) from a JSON file.

buttons.label: Save scheme
buttons.description: Export the state labels, every non-zero transition rate and the brightness as a JSON scheme file.

sections.description: Session files, the guided tour and the help.

buttons.label: Load session
buttons.description: Restore the optics, kinetics and display settings saved by Save session.

buttons.label: Save session
buttons.description: Save the optics, kinetics and display settings to the per-user settings file, which is read again when the tool starts.

buttons.label: Guide
buttons.description: A step-by-step walk through a worked example: Rhodamine 6G at 488 nm.

buttons.label: Help
buttons.description: Explain saturation, the scheme matrices and how to read the curves.

sections.title: Photophysics
sections.description: The scheme, the excitation and the measurement settings.

sections.label: Scheme
sections.description: Load a photophysical scheme. Presets are starting points, not constraints: every rate, cross-section and brightness stays editable.

sections.label: Laser power
sections.description: Total laser power measured at the objective (mW). It sets the photon flux and with it the peak excitation rate k_exc(0,0) = 2 sigma Phi / (pi w_r^2). At 0 the saturated curve is exactly the unsaturated Gaussian. Type a value or use the arrows.

sections.label: Power (log)
sections.description: The same power on a logarithmic scale from 0.001 to 100 mW (the exponent is shown), because the interesting range spans decades.

sections.label: Excitation λ
sections.description: Excitation wavelength. It sets the photon energy, so the same power delivers more photons at longer wavelengths, and the extinction read from a chosen dye.

sections.label: Dye (MMFDB)
sections.description: Read the extinction coefficient at the excitation wavelength from the dye's stored absorption spectrum in MMFDB. Leave empty to type the extinction in the Optics table.

sections.label: Rate units
sections.description: Time base of the dark transition rates. Changing it rescales the entered values, it does not reinterpret them.

sections.label: Bunching dynamics
sections.description: Include the photokinetic bunching factor in the saturated curve: the relaxation of the scheme on the diffusion timescale.

sections.label: Number of states
sections.description: Number of states of the scheme. Two is the minimum (ground and excited); add one for each dark, isomeric or bleached state.

sections.name: k_dark
sections.description: Power-independent dark transition rates K_dark: the row is the state a transition starts from, the column the state it ends in, in the rate units above. The ground-state row is the excitation (use K_exc) and the diagonal is not a rate. Double click a cell to type a value; zero removes the transition.

sections.name: k_exc
sections.description: Excitation cross-sections K_exc relative to the peak excitation rate: row is the state a transition starts from, column the state it ends in. Double click a cell to type a value between 0 and 1.

sections.name: brightness
sections.description: Relative brightness Q of every state: the fluorescence a molecule emits while in it. Dark states have zero.

sections.name: optics
sections.description: Optics and measurement: power P, wavelength, extinction epsilon, beam waists w_r and w_z, diffusion coefficient D, number of molecules N, offset b and background bg. The relaxation times tau_R of the scheme are results and cannot be edited.

items.label: Normalize G(τ) to 1.0
items.description: Scale both curves to G(0) = 1 to compare their shapes: the saturated curve is not only smaller but broader.

items.label: 1-component fit
items.description: Overlay the best single-component 3D Gaussian fit of the saturated curve, what a standard FCS analysis would report.

sections.description: Which curves the radial profile plot shows.

sections.label: Excitation k(r)
sections.description: Show the excitation rate profile across the focus, relative to its peak.

sections.label: State populations
sections.description: Show the fraction of molecules in every state as a function of the radial position.

sections.label: Emission Σ Q·P
sections.description: Show the emission profile, the sum of the state brightnesses times their populations.
